Both answers come from git runs on the two branches.

- **Ancestor:** No. `git merge-base --is-ancestor side HEAD` on `feat/2.1.327-next` printed `NOT-ANCESTOR`. The two branches diverged from `3e7e491de`.
- **Conflict:** Yes. `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD side` exited 1 with `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in plans/rebuild/README.md`. It is a dry run that writes no merge commit and doesn't touch the working tree.

Both commits are in place and nothing was merged:
- `side` has `fb56fbda6`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (side)`.
- `feat/2.1.327-next` has `6ac4a2108`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (next)`.
- You are back on `feat/2.1.327-next`.

The graph also shows two older commits, `702f2148a` and `579054ee7`, on other refs. They also retitle the rebuild README and come from earlier runs, not this one. I didn't touch them. The tree was clean before and after.
